title: Chow groups with modulus versus Suslin homology for smooth projective varieties over perfect fields with regular reduced-divisor components, after inverting positive characteristic or modulo nonzero integers in characteristic zero
author: Federico Binda; Amalendu Krishna
difficulty_reason: The cited nilpotent-invariance theorem does not turn an arbitrary Suslin rational-equivalence relation into an admissible modulus relation on the given variety. The authors embed the normalization curve into a projective bundle and construct blowups that enforce the required transverse intersections with the regular divisor components. That geometric reduction and the final comparison of the two relation presentations establish the isomorphism with the specified coefficients.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Exact Theorem4.5, equivalently1.2: perfect base field, smooth projective variety, effective Cartier divisor whose reduced irreducible components are regular; coefficient ring Z[1/p] when characteristic p>0, or Z/m for nonzero integer m in characteristic0. Both regimes are a single comparison theorem, not two units. Source notation R=[1/p] on25 means the previously specified Z[1/p]. Integral algebraically closed-field comparison1.1 and singular-normal-crossing motivic comparison1.6 are not included. Full new embedding/pushforward diagram, divisor-preserving blow-ups, transverse normalization and final relation comparison read. Existing Suslin relation presentation, proper functoriality of modulus Chow groups, Jannsen transverse blow-up theorem and Miyazaki modulus reduction are explicitly cited research foundations. Ambient smoothness and regularity of each reduced divisor component, rather than a claim for arbitrary singular divisors, retained in title and packet. No cuspidal characteristic-zero computation with details left to reader selected.
